mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-18.1, -16.6, -17.6, -14.1 with net improvement), indicating a persistent recovery momentum in retail footfall that will continue mechanically over the next four weeks absent new shocks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -18.1 at t-3w to -14.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days, indicating momentum reversed rather than continued.

mechanism_narrative: Once WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -5 percent (near-normal commuting levels), eased workplace restrictions spill over into lunchtime and after-work retail activity, pulling RETAIL_REC upward within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -5.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -4.3 at t-0w, just below the -5 threshold
regime_hint: phased reopening with workplace restrictions easing
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within two weeks after WORKPLACES crosses above -5, or RETAIL_REC declines despite WORKPLACES remaining above -5.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES reflects restored commuting behavior; when both series rise together week-on-week, the combined effect of transit access and workplace attendance amplifies discretionary retail trips beyond what either series predicts alone, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -23.0 to -19.1 and WORKPLACES from -8.7 to -4.3 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in weeks where both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise simultaneously relative to the prior week, breaking the interaction claim.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 10.7 to 8.3 over four weeks, indicating people are spending less time at home; this freed-up time converts into discretionary outings, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks, but only while the broader reopening regime holds.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 10.7 at t-3w to 8.3 at t-0w
regime_hint: reopening with continued easing of stay-home measures
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its decline, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward and RETAIL_REC still rises, decoupling the mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high week-to-week volatility (-21.0, -22.0, -26.6, -20.6), consistent with weather-driven weekend outdoor activity substituting for retail trips; when PARKS spikes upward by more than 5 points week-on-week, RETAIL_REC growth is temporarily dampened the following week as outdoor substitution absorbs discretionary time.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -26.6 at t-1w to -20.6 at t-0w, a 6-point jump
regime_hint: reopening with good weather and outdoor options available
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following a PARKS spike greater than 5 points, contradicting the substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: Singapore's phased reopening caps the pace of retail recovery; once RETAIL_REC approaches within 10 points of baseline (i.e., exceeds -10), further gains decelerate sharply because remaining restrictions (capacity limits, safe-distancing) bind, causing RETAIL_REC to plateau rather than continue its prior rate of improvement.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises above -10.0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at -14.1 is approaching the -10 policy-binding threshold
regime_hint: phased reopening with capacity restrictions still in force
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising at the same or faster rate after crossing -10, showing no deceleration, or it plateaus well before reaching -10.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM turned positive for the first time in this snapshot (2.6 at t-0w versus negative values in prior weeks), signaling behavioral normalization of errand trips; this normalization pattern typically precedes a broader rise in non-essential retail visits within two weeks as consumer confidence in public spaces returns.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -2.0 at t-1w to 2.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM crossing above 0, or it declines despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement of TRANSIT (less negative) and decline in RESIDENTIAL together indicate reduced home-confinement and restored mobility infrastructure use; their combined trend, rather than either alone, drives a sustained four-week rise in RETAIL_REC because both enabling (transit) and motivational (less home time) conditions must co-occur.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -23.0 to -19.1 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 10.7 to 8.3 over the same four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks even though TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL both move in the enabling direction simultaneously, or RETAIL_REC rises despite only one of the two series moving favorably.
